subject: Supply Chain & Logistics
title: Delivery Density
description: A micro-lesson that makes Delivery Density usable.

hook.text: In Manhattan, a driver delivers 120 packages per day. In rural Montana, the same driver delivers 20.

buildup.text: Delivery density—packages per square mile—is the biggest driver of last-mile cost and efficiency.

discovery.text: Dense urban areas allow more stops per hour. Sparse rural areas mean long drives between each drop.

twist.text: Customers everywhere expect the same delivery speed. But the economics of rural delivery are brutal.

climax.text: Companies use zone pricing, pickup points, and delivery days to make low-density areas viable.

punchline.text: More packages per mile means lower cost per package.

quiz.question: What makes rural last-mile delivery so expensive?
options: Low delivery density—long drives between stops
